newsitem.title: USA: U.S. domestic crude grade differentials weaken.
newsitem.headline: U.S. domestic crude grade differentials weaken.

text.p: U.S. crude grade differentials slipped slightly through the afternoon Tuesday, retreating from overdone price levels, traders said.

November outright prices firmed from earlier losses, led by a recovery in gasoline prices and by the lack of further confirmation the Iraqi oil-for-food deal with the United Nations was any closer to implementation.

Earlier, reports said U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros Ghali had informed Turkish leaders Iraqi oil exports would be starting in a matter of a few weeks. The U.S. has not responded to the reports, alleviating some pressure on crude.

Gasoline futures prices spiked higher on reports Conoco's Lake Charles, La., refinery was shut due to a fire. However, Conoco later said the 180,000 barrel per day refinery was not shut by the fire, and all units were operating normally.
Conoco's statement defused the rally in gasoline shortly thereafter, said sources.
November West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was valued at $24.25-$24.35, around 5 cts weaker from the close on Monday.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was traded at 35 cts and 36 cts over WTI/Cushing, with last talk at 34-36 cts above WTI/Cushing.
Midland/WTI was quiet at 4-6 cts over WTI/Cushing.
West Texas Sour/Midland was last done at 28 cts under WTI.

Traders said the deflation in grade values was based mainly on the market being overbought. Sour grades were hit a little harder than the sweet parcels, traders said, noting some major refiners entered the fray this morning to fill out requirements.

Foreign crude business to the U.S. was subdued. The only cargoes seen coming in the near future from the North Sea, was an 80,000 tonne loader from the Alba field for delivery to the U.S. Gulf on November 1, traders said.
